clauses.reason: The clause restates the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10084 so that the order ceases to be effective on March 31, 1950 instead of January 31, 1950. Under the owner ruling on restatements the clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends. Executive Orders 10118, 10136, 10158 and 10174 restated or extended that sunset in turn, each recorded as a later event with its date; as last amended by Executive Order 10174 the parent continues, for section 302 regulations, “until January 31, 1951”, so the clause ends on January 31, 1951 (inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins). Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Each amendment takes effect the day after the earlier date it extends ends, so the dates are read inclusively and leave no gap.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10098 (15 FR 461 (Federal Register of January 27, 1950)) concerns the order that adopts, as regulations under Titles II, III and V of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, the existing pay regulations, and fixes how long that adoption lasts. Executive Order 10098 was signed January 25, 1950. Its only command amends the last paragraph of Executive Order No. 10084 to read that the order takes effect October 1, 1949 and ceases to be effective on March 31, 1950, replacing the January 31, 1950 sunset. Sunset text by instrument: Executive Order 10084 (October 12, 1949): the order shall cease to be effective on January 31, 1950. Executive Order 10098 (signed January 25, 1950): the last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950. Executive Order 10118 (signed March 27, 1950): last paragraph restated, ceasing March 31, 1950 except that, to the extent it adopts regulations under sections 201(e), 204, 206, 302 and 501(d) of the Career Compensation Act of 1949, it continues until June 30, 1950. Executive Order 10136 (signed June 30, 1950, effective July 1, 1950): sections 201(e), 204, 206 and 501(d) continue until August 31, 1950 and section 302 until September 30, 1950. Executive Order 10158 (signed August 31, 1950, effective September 1, 1950): sections 206 and 302 continue until October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (signed October 23, 1950, effective November 1, 1950): section 302 continues until January 31, 1951. Effective dates are read as follows. Executive Order 10098 and Executive Order 10118 state no effective date and are recorded as effective on their signing dates, January 25, 1950 and March 27, 1950, which fall before the January 31, 1950 and March 31, 1950 sunsets they restate, so each replaced the sunset then running. Executive Order 10136 (effective July 1, 1950) takes effect the day after June 30, 1950, the date to which Executive Order 10118 continued the listed sections. Executive Order 10158 (effective September 1, 1950) takes effect the day after August 31, 1950, the date to which Executive Order 10136 continued section 206, but before September 30, 1950, the date to which Executive Order 10136 continued section 302, so for section 302 it replaced the September 30 date with October 31, 1950. Executive Order 10174 (effective November 1, 1950) takes effect the day after October 31, 1950. Only Executive Orders 10136 and 10174 take effect after the date they extend. The stated end dates are read inclusively; the exclusive reading would end each continuation when its stated day begins. The last held instrument is Executive Order 10174 (15 FR 7165 (Federal Register of October 26, 1950)), which continues the order, to the extent it adopts regulations under section 302 of the Act, “until January 31, 1951”. On 2026-10-14 the clause is terminated at that last sunset, January 31, 1951, inclusive; the exclusive reading would end it when that day begins. The dossier's later-event chain and the held-text search for citations of Executive Order No. 10084 (searched also with a trailing footnote digit) show no later instrument after Executive Order 10174: the Federal Register disposition-note search lists the five amendments named above, and the U.S. Code and eCFR citation searches report no hit. A later extension that the held corpus lacks is not excluded, which is the usual limit of a bounded search and is disclosed.

savings.reason: The order's text has no saving clause. Pay and allowances earned under the regulations while they were adopted are entitlements under the Career Compensation Act of 1949 and the regulations then in force; the held text creates no continuing duty after January 31, 1951, and the bounded searches found no later order continuing or restoring the adoption.
